subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main job of decomposers in nutrient cycling?
options: They break down dead organisms and release nutrients into the soil
They prevent nutrients from entering the soil
They hunt and eat primary consumers
They produce energy from the Sun
questions.explain: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to reuse.

questions.q: Longshore drift is the process that:
options: Transports sediment ALONG the coast in a zig-zag motion
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast as swash arrives at an angle and backwash returns straight down.

questions.q: Why are tropical rainforests so important for the global environment?
options: They reflect sunlight back into space
They store carbon and produce oxygen
They cool the planet by producing ice
questions.explain: Rainforests act as a carbon store and 'carbon sink', and their photosynthesis releases oxygen, helping regulate the climate.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: Groynes are wooden or rock barriers built out into the sea in order to:
options: Trap sediment and build up the beach
questions.explain: Groynes interrupt longshore drift, trapping sediment to widen the beach.

questions.q: The coastal erosion process where waves throw pebbles against a cliff, wearing it away, is:
questions.explain: Abrasion occurs as waves hurl sediment against the cliff, grinding it away.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
A thick, waxy stem to store water
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, which of these is an abiotic component?
questions.explain: Abiotic means the non-living physical parts of an ecosystem, such as temperature, water, light and soil.

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: Which of these is an opportunity provided by a hot desert environment?
questions.explain: The intense, reliable sunshine of hot deserts makes them ideal for generating solar power.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.
